standard.title: Unidirectional Non-Woven Semi-Cured Glass Fibre Tape — Specification (एकदिशीय गैर-बुना अर्ध-पका हुआ ग्लास फाइबर टेप — विशिष्टि)

sectional_committee.name: Solid Electrical Insulating Materials Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the quality, material, constructional, and performance-testing specifications for unidirectional non-woven glass fabric tape consisting of parallel twisted glass yarns designed to bandage armatures of rotating machines and transformer coils to hold assembly windings securely in position.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the quality, material, constructional, and performance-testing specifications for unidirectional non-woven glass fabric tape consisting of parallel twisted glass yarns designed to bandage armatures of rotating machines and transformer coils to hold assembly windings securely in position.

supersedes: None (Developed as a new dedicated specification for resin-impregnated glass banding tapes)

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or emboss the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the product rolls or boxes to certify dimensional, thermal, and metallurgical conformity.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, thickness tolerances, storage temperatures, and weight loss percentages must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The tape must consist of parallel twisted glass yarns aligned in a unidirectional non-woven pattern to provide maximum longitudinal tensile strength.
The glass yarns must be constructed of continuous E-glass fibers containing not more than one percent of alkali calculated as sodium oxide.

The fiber tape must be impregnated with catalyzed thermosetting synthetic resins (such as acrylic, polyester, or epoxy compounds) and semi-cured to a suitable B-stage to ensure optimal flow and tack-free handling during winding.

Because the tape is semi-cured, storage temperature governs shelf life: 10°C storage provides 18 months of shelf life; 15°C storage provides 12 months; and 20°C storage provides 8 months. Normally, the manufacturing date must not be earlier than one month from dispatch.
Preferred nominal thicknesses are 0.3 or 0.33 mm. The measured thickness must not deviate from the nominal value by more than ± 0.05 mm.

Thickness is measured using a micrometer with 0.01 mm accuracy under 10 N/cm² pressure, on 5 rolls selected at random conditioned as per IS 196 (65 ± 2% RH and 27 ± 2 °C). Ten measurements are taken every 300 mm.

Three 1 m specimens are cut, weighed, and heated in an oven at a temperature 20°C higher than the designated thermal class of the tape for 400 hours ± 30 minutes, cooled in a desiccator, and reweighed. Weight loss must satisfy low, specified limits to ensure resin stability.
